subject: beewolf wasp
title: A Wasp Hunts Honeybees and Grows Antibiotics in Its Antennae

scenes.text: This wasp grows medicine in its antennae.
The European beewolf hunts honeybees. One sting behind the front legs, and the bee is paralyzed.
She flies it to her burrow and packs up to five bees in each nursery cell.
But a damp burrow full of bees is a feast for mold.
So she squeezes a white paste from her antennae onto the ceiling. It's alive: bacteria that make antibiotics.
Her larva eats the bees, then weaves the bacteria into its cocoon. Without them, almost none survive.

description:
The European beewolf is a solitary wasp that hunts honeybees and protects its young with antibiotic-making bacteria.
The female stings a honeybee through the soft membrane behind its front legs, carries the paralyzed bee in flight to a burrow up to a meter long, and stocks each brood cell with one to five bees; one female may collect up to 100. Before sealing a cell she smears its ceiling with a whitish secretion from glands in her antennae that is full of Streptomyces bacteria. The larva takes the bacteria up and works them into the silk of its cocoon, where they keep fungus off. In experiments reported in Current Biology in 2005, larvae without the bacteria rarely survived.
Which insect do you think is the smartest parent? Comment below.
first_comment: Beewolves nest together in sandy ground, sometimes as many as 15,000 burrows in one spot. Which insect do you think is the smartest parent?
